findings.title: Elevation as event, measure, and valued scale
findings.claim: With taʿālā restated by the cognate measure ʿuluwwan and enlarged as kabīran, elevation is both predicated and measured, with no commensurate upper limit relative to the speech at issue.
findings.mechanism: The two elw forms carry the elevation, their cognate relation restates the verb as a nominal measure, and the separate kbr adjective enlarges that measure. The governed saying supplies the comparison-domain, changing height from a single location into a valued scale above speech.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader perceives elevation as both an asserted state and an explicit scale, with rank and magnitude available together.
findings.containment: All HFT roles are attributed and legacy-unbound. The vertical image is not physical ascent, rank is not a human office, and no numerical upper bound is asserted.
